extraction.command:
python3 -c 'import re,html,sys
p=sys.argv[1]
t=open(p,encoding="utf-8",errors="replace").read()
t=re.sub(r"(?is)\x3c(script|style|noscript)[^\x3e]*\x3e.*?\x3c/\1\x3e"," ",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3cbr\s*/?\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3c/(p|div|li|h[1-6]|tr|section|article)\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?s)\x3c[^\x3e]+\x3e"," ",t)
t=html.unescape(t)
t="\n".join(re.sub(r"[ \t\xa0]+"," ",l).strip() for l in t.split("\n"))
t=re.sub(r"\n{3,}","\n\n",t).strip()+"\n"
sys.stdout.write(t)' content/sources/kmk-home.html

knownStaleness.topic: This page does NOT state that Halifax is in Mi'kma'ki, and that is the finding
knownStaleness.problem: Until 2026-09-14, content/levels/halifax.json's statement opened `Halifax is in Mi'kma'ki, the territory of the Mi'kmaq` and cited this home page as its `nationSource`. A verifier rejected that statement. It now cites content/sources/kmk-about-consultation.json for both its fact and its nation name, and no longer uses the word `Mi'kma'ki`. The finding below is kept because it is why. Both words are on this page and neither is used to make that claim. `Mi’kma’ki` appears six times and every one of them is a press-release DATELINE or a headline about spraying - `Mi’kma’ki – Maw-lukutijik Saqmaq (Assembly) is calling for meaningful consultation`, `Assembly Opposes Planned Glyphosate Spraying in Mi’kma’ki` - the way a release from Ottawa is datelined Ottawa. `Halifax` appears exactly once, also as a dateline: `Halifax, Nova Scotia – Chief Sidney Peters, Glooscap First Nation and Chief Leroy Denny, Eskasoni First Nation`. The words `territory` and `unceded` do not appear on the page at all. There is no sentence here placing Halifax, or any other named place, inside Mi'kma'ki. The strongest territorial sentences the page does carry are `We have never surrendered, ceded or sold the Aboriginal Title to any lands and resources in Nova Scotia` and `We work on behalf of the Mi’kmaq of Nova Scotia`, both of which are about Nova Scotia rather than about Halifax.
knownStaleness.action: this register supports the NAME `Mi'kmaq` and nothing more. Do not read a dateline as a territorial assertion: the Assembly datelining its own releases `Mi’kma’ki` is the Assembly saying where it speaks from, and turning that into `Halifax is in Mi'kma'ki` would be the project making the claim in the Assembly's name. Whether the halifax statement can be repaired at all is a question for whoever revises it, and the answer this cache gives is no - not from this page, and not from content/sources/kmk-about-consultation.json either, which contains one `Mi’kma’ki` and no `Halifax`.

knownStaleness.topic: A home page that is mostly a live news feed
knownStaleness.problem: Most of this page's 14 KB of text is the organisation's current news, media releases and newsletters. At the time of caching the newest item was dated `[September 11, 2026]` - two days before this fetch. `extractedTextSha256` will therefore stop matching within days, for reasons that have nothing to do with the standing text. The standing text - the `PJILA’SI` welcome, the `About Us` paragraph, the Five Pillars, the `Key Accomplishments` list - does not move.
knownStaleness.action: when the digest stops matching, re-read the `About Us` paragraph beginning `We work on behalf of the Mi’kmaq of Nova Scotia` before assuming anything moved. Expect this register to need re-fetching more often than any other in this directory, and expect the re-fetch to find the same standing text under a different news list.

knownStaleness.topic: The apostrophe is U+2019 throughout, and the level documents use U+0027
knownStaleness.problem: This site writes `Mi’kmaq`, `Mi’kma’ki`, `Kwilmu’kw` and `PJILA’SI` with the right single quotation mark. content/levels/halifax.json and content/levels/peggys-cove.json write `Mi'kmaq` with the ASCII apostrophe. A containment check that compares the level's `nations` entry against these bytes literally will therefore MISS, and a verifier who normalises before comparing has quietly edited a nation's own orthography to make a check pass.
knownStaleness.action: compare deliberately, and record which form was compared. Do not rewrite either side to match the other without saying so: docs/content-review.md 9.3 says the diacritics and orthography are copied exactly from the nationSource, which means the question of which apostrophe this project ships is a real one and not a normalisation detail.

grainNote: One web page, four headings taken from the page's own h1/h2 elements. Flags at chapter grain because a home page has no pages to point at. The first flag is the whole reason this register exists: the level that cites this URL makes a claim the URL does not make, and recording that is more use than caching the page quietly and leaving the next reader to discover it.
